scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. I'm 33 years old and have been living with my parents most of my life. They charge me $200, which is market rate where we live, so that seems fair. I pay rent, which helps, and I have everything I need without the hassle of finding a new place. We mostly get along, but I tend to avoid them a lot. Recently, there was a toilet flood in my bathroom, which means they had to remodel my section of the house. Because of this, we're running into each other a lot more than before. I used to lock myself in my room most of the time to avoid them, but now that's not possible. Today, my parents went to Costco. When they got home, I was sitting on the couch playing Apex Legends. My mom asked me to get up and help them bring in the groceries. I told her I'd do it in a minute. I was too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth. Finally, my dad told me to get my ass up, and I told him I'd do it in a minute. He said, "A minute is now," grabbed the controller out of my hand, and it turned into a huge shouting match. Now, they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday, which is basically impossible. They also brought up my younger brother, who is married with two kids and just got promoted at his job. They have their "golden child," and now they're throwing his success in my face. I mean, I guess I could have gotten up and helped them, but to me, because I pay rent, that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yardwork. Am I the asshole in this situation? Alright, so I need to figure out if I'm the asshole here. Let's break it down. First, I'm an adult paying rent, which is fair. I have a right to live there, and I contribute financially. However, I'm still living with my parents, which is not typical for someone my age. That might be part of the issue. When my parents asked me to help with groceries, I was playing a video game and told them I'd do it in a minute. They ended up making several trips, and my dad got frustrated, leading to a shouting match. Now, they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to find a place by Friday, which seems unrealistic. I also feel that they're comparing me to my younger brother, who is married with kids and has a good job. That's probably making me feel worse about myself. I'm paying rent, so I feel like I have the right to say no to helping with chores or errands. But is that fair? On one hand, I'm contributing financially, which is important. On the other hand, living with others usually comes with some responsibilities, like helping out with household tasks. My parents might feel that I'm not pulling my weight beyond just paying rent. Also, the fact that I was avoiding them and now, because of the remodel, we're interacting more, might have contributed to the tension. My dad grabbed the controller, which probably escalated the situation. So, am I the asshole? Well, I think there's a bit of both sides. I'm an adult paying rent, but living with parents usually implies some level of shared responsibilities. Refusing to help with groceries when asked, especially when it's a family effort, might be seen as selfish. Also, the way I responded, by saying I'd do it in a minute and then not doing it, could have come off as dismissive. However, my parents might also be overreacting by checking into a hotel and expecting me to find a place in such a short time. That seems extreme, especially since I'm already contributing financially. In the end, communication seems to be the key issue here. Both sides could have handled the situation better. I could have been more considerate of their needs and responded more promptly, while they could have communicated their frustration more calmly and not set an unrealistic deadline. So, I think I'm partially the asshole for not helping out when asked and for the way I responded, but my parents also share some responsibility for how they handled the situation.
